sources.quote: In tonal notation, / represents downstep, while v( represents any vowel bearing the infralow tone in the four-register Yendang system. (Given the provisional nature of the Momi data, these are noted without tones.)
sources.locator: Part I ('Tiba I, 30/11/99'), notation paragraph immediately preceding 'LIST 1: Adamawa cognates for Tiba nouns'; Yendang data statement (typescript p. 4) and footnote 3
sources.note: In the notation paragraph before List 1 Boyd states that Yendang has a four-register tone system including an 'infralow' tone (marked with a special diacritic on his Yendang forms), and uses '/' for downstep; his Yendang citations in Lists 1-2 are tone-marked accordingly. This is a passing but explicit first-hand characterisation (4 level tones), the only published statement of the Yendang tone inventory located; Zheltov 2020/2022 (a work listed here) mark only H/M/L provisionally and call their tonal notation 'very preliminary'.
